findings.description: The inline policy grants wildcard actions (ec2:*, s3:*, lambda:*, cloudwatch:*) on Resource "*" to a long-lived IAM user. This violates least privilege, grants unconditional access to all S3 data and all compute in the account, and enables privilege escalation (e.g. via lambda:*/ec2 to assume higher-privileged roles or exfiltrate data). Any compromise of this user's static credentials yields full control over storage and compute.

The output publishes the access key's secret material (aws_iam_access_key.svc_deploy_key.encrypted_secret) without `sensitive = true`, so it is rendered in CLI/plan output and persisted in readable Terraform state. Combined with the accompanying static key pair, this leaks deploy credentials to anyone with plan/state access.

A permanent, non-rotating access key is created for the svc_deploy IAM user. Static long-lived keys that grant wildcard ec2/s3/lambda/cloudwatch permissions are a high-value credential that cannot be scoped, expires only manually, and is stored in Terraform state; a role with temporary STS credentials would be the secure alternative.
